The government has assured the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) of its commitment to protecting the institution’s technical independence, saying its regulatory decisions must remain free from external interference.
Chief Director of the Ministry of Health, Desmond Boateng, gave the assurance on behalf of Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh at the launch of the FDA’s 30th anniversary celebrations.
He said government would provide the Authority with the support and resources needed to strengthen its regulatory capacity.
Mr Boateng said the FDA’s independence was essential to ensuring that decisions on the safety and quality of regulated products were guided by scientific evidence, public safety and the national interest.
“As a government, we guarantee the FDA absolute technical independence in this endeavour. A trusted regulator is one whose decisions are guided solely by public safety and the national interest, free from external interference,” he said.
The minister’s address also raised concerns about the circulation of illicit, counterfeit, substandard, falsified and unregistered products on the Ghanaian market.
He warned that such products posed a serious threat to public health and could undermine the quality of healthcare.
“The proliferation of illicit and fake products on our markets poses a direct lethal threat to unsuspecting citizens and undermines our clinical care outcomes,” he said.
Mr Boateng identified the growing use of social media and e-commerce platforms to market unapproved and expired products as a major regulatory challenge.
He said the trend was creating gaps in oversight and exposing consumers, particularly young people, to potentially unsafe products.
He therefore urged the FDA to intensify market surveillance, strengthen controls at ports and borders, expand laboratory testing and enforce sanctions under the Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851).
He also called for the adoption of modern tracking systems and digital platforms to monitor products across supply chains and help verify their authenticity.
The government’s assurance comes as the FDA marks 30 years of regulating the safety and quality of products under its mandate.
